h2: Ultrasonic testing in Baton Rouge: turnaround thickness work and Louisiana's rules
html:
Ultrasonic testing in Baton Rouge: turnaround thickness work and Louisiana's rules

In Baton Rouge, ultrasonic testing mostly supports refinery and chemical plant integrity programs along the Mississippi River: thickness readings at piping and vessel condition monitoring locations, weld examination on turnaround repairs, and corrosion mapping where localized loss is suspected. Crews travel from Houston, and an ASNT NDT Level III reviews the procedures, data and reports.

Thickness data that holds up. Under API 570 and API 510, the owner's inspector uses measured corrosion rates to set remaining life and the next inspection date, so the value of a UT survey is in its repeatability. The same condition monitoring location, probe type and calibration approach should be used every campaign, and readings on hot lines need high-temperature couplant, a probe rated for the surface temperature and a correction for the change in sound velocity. Atlantis performs the NDE and the data review for the owner's program; it is not an Authorized Inspector and does not sign as inspector of record.

Where UT goes in river-corridor plants.

  • Thickness surveys at elbows, tees, injection points and dead legs in crude, hydrotreating and chemical units
  • Automated corrosion mapping on vessel shells and large-bore piping where spot readings would miss pitting
  • Angle-beam and phased array screening for wet hydrogen sulfide cracking in sour water, amine and similar services
  • Shear-wave or PAUT examination of repair and replacement welds before a unit returns to service
  • Thickness checks on insulated lines after corrosion under insulation is found, a common finding in the region's heat and humidity

Turnaround timing. Gulf Coast plants generally plan turnarounds outside the peak summer demand period, and the Atlantic hurricane season runs from June 1 to November 30, so spring work packages fill early. UT scopes that are written, with locations marked on isometrics, before the unit comes down are the ones that finish on schedule.

Which rules apply in Louisiana. Louisiana is not an OSHA State Plan state, so federal OSHA's process safety management standard governs covered units, and its mechanical integrity element requires inspection and testing of process equipment to recognized and generally accepted good engineering practice, which is where API 510 and API 570 come in. Boilers come under the Mechanical Safety Section of the Louisiana State Fire Marshal's Office. Radiography in Louisiana is licensed by the state, which is an NRC Agreement State; phased array or TOFD can keep a radiation boundary off a busy unit where the code allows UT in its place.

The method is explained on the ultrasonic testing page, mapping on the automated UT page, and outage support on the turnaround and shutdown inspection page. Piping owners can see how NDE supports their inspector on the API 570 piping NDE support page, and Atlantis ERP keeps readings tied to the same locations each campaign. Technicians starting out can look at UT Level I in Baton Rouge and UT training. To scope a survey, send isometrics, CML lists and dates through the Baton Rouge UT request.
